claim: For an odd electorate of size \(n=2m+1\), with a quota requiring at least \(r=m+1+s\) affirmative final votes, \(0\le s\le m\), suppose every voter independently chooses uniformly among voting yes, voting no, and delegating to each available out-neighbor. Starting from no delegation edges, add the single edge \(a\to b\). Let \(M_i\) be the unnormalized probability that forcing voter \(i\)'s direct vote from no to yes changes the quota outcome, with all other actions drawn from this model, and set \(B_{n,r}=\binom{n-1}{r-1}/2^{n-1}\). Then \(M_a=B_{n,r}\), \(M_b=4B_{n,r}/3\), and for every \(c\notin\{a,b\}\), \(M_c=B_{n,r}(2/3+R_{n,r}/3)\), where \(R_{n,r}=2[\binom{n-3}{r-1}+\binom{n-3}{r-3}]/\binom{n-1}{r-1}=(n-3)/(n-2)+2s^2/[m(n-2)]\), with out-of-range binomial coefficients interpreted as zero. Consequently, \(\sum_i M_i=nB_{n,r}+2s^2B_{n,r}/(3m)\): aggregate unnormalized criticality is conserved exactly at simple majority and strictly increases for every stricter supermajority quota.

scientific_limitations_and_integrity.integrity: Analytic proof plus exact standard-library enumeration checks; general a-priori power-index framework is prior art. Independent audit and independent validation have not been performed.
scientific_limitations_and_integrity.limitations: Unit weights, odd electorate, deterministic integer quota, independent uniform actions, one acyclic delegation edge only. No claim about arbitrary graph edits, weighted voters, even electorates, correlated choices, cycles, strategic behavior, welfare, or truth-tracking accuracy.

title: Exact one-edge power redistribution under quota voting
